result.summary: Corrects the offset and byte width used when parsing NAT-PMP result codes during Port Control Protocol (PCP) fallback in `pcp.cpp`. Instead of reading a single byte using a PCP header offset constant, the code now reads a 16-bit big-endian integer at the NAT-PMP result offset. A unit test is also added to `pcp_tests.cpp`.
result.problem: When handling a potential NAT-PMP unsupported version response from a gateway, `PCPRequestPortMap` evaluated a single byte at offset 3 rather than a 16-bit big-endian value at offset 2. A 16-bit result code ending in byte 1 with a non-zero high byte (such as 0x0101) would be falsely interpreted as `UNSUPP_VERSION`.
evidence: PR description and commit cite RFC 6887 Appendix A and RFC 6886 Section 3.5 regarding 16-bit big-endian NAT-PMP result code layout
Author points to internal inconsistency with other NAT-PMP response parsing at lines 348 and 390 of `src/common/pcp.cpp`
result.scope_notes: Small fix accompanied by a unit test in `pcp_tests.cpp`.
result.card: Fixes a header parsing bug in Port Control Protocol (PCP) port mapping when checking for NAT-PMP gateway fallback. `PCPRequestPortMap` checked a single byte at offset 3 instead of reading a 16-bit big-endian result code starting at offset 2, causing result codes like 0x0101 to be falsely treated as unsupported-version errors. The author points out inconsistency with existing NAT-PMP parsing in `pcp.cpp` and cites RFC 6886/6887 specifications. The change includes a unit test in `pcp_tests.cpp`.

risk.why: A mistake would only affect automated gateway port-mapping negotiation for nodes behind NAT gateways that support PCP and NAT-PMP.
